taxonomies.name: Range Upper-Bound Inclusion
taxonomies.description: Learner believes that range(start, stop) includes the upper bound (stop value) in the generated sequence.
observable_signals: Explicitly predicts the stop value in loop output
Predicts stop - start + 1 iterations instead of stop - start
Phrasing indicates inclusive interval such as 'from start through stop' or 'up to and including'
taxonomies.common_reasoning: range(1, 5) means numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 because 5 is specified as the end.
taxonomies.counterexample: range(1, 4) produces exactly 3 elements: [1, 2, 3]. Notice 4 is never reached.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Present an unseen range with different start, stop, and step values to confirm boundary exclusion.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Learner correctly identifies output sequence without including stop value on 2 consecutive unseen problems.

taxonomies.name: Off-by-One Iteration Count
taxonomies.description: Learner miscounts total loop iterations by confounding 0-based counting with 1-based cardinality or misinterpreting loop bounds.
observable_signals: Predicts N+1 or N-1 executions for range(N)
Understands that range is exclusive but miscalculates the count
Counts 0 as the 1st iteration but then adds N at the end
taxonomies.common_reasoning: for i in range(5) will print 6 times because it starts at 0 and goes to 5.
taxonomies.counterexample: range(5) outputs: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Count them on your fingers: that is exactly 5 items.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Present loop counter problems testing total iteration count across 0-indexed ranges.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Accurately predicts total iterations on unseen zero-indexed and offset loops.

taxonomies.name: Assignment vs Equality Operator
taxonomies.description: Learner confuses the assignment operator (=) with the equality comparison operator (==) in conditional statements.
observable_signals: Writes 'if x = 5:' to test equality
Believes that '=' checks if two expressions have identical values
Confuses syntax error in Python with true/false evaluation
taxonomies.common_reasoning: In math, x = 5 checks if x is equal to 5, so if x = 5 should evaluate to true.
taxonomies.counterexample: x = 5 is an ACTION (store 5 into x). x == 5 is a QUESTION (is x equal to 5?). Python forbids '=' in if-conditions.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Ask learner to write or evaluate conditional checks distinguishing assignment from comparison.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Consistently uses '==' for condition checks and '=' strictly for variable assignment.

taxonomies.name: Variable Scope Shadowing
taxonomies.description: Learner believes assigning to a variable with the same name inside a local function scope permanently alters the enclosing global variable.
observable_signals: Predicts the global variable value changed after calling a function without 'global'
Unaware of local variable creation and lexical scope shielding
Believes identical variable names across functions refer to the same shared memory
taxonomies.common_reasoning: Inside the function we set x = 10, so outside x must now be 10.
taxonomies.counterexample: Assigning x = 10 inside def f(): creates a brand-new local variable. The outside x remains untouched.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Present multi-scope code execution traces without the global keyword.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Correctly separates local variable bindings from global scope across unseen function calls.

taxonomies.name: Missing Base Case in Recursion
taxonomies.description: Learner believes a recursive function naturally stops when a counter reaches zero or when an argument finishes, without an explicit base case guard.
observable_signals: Writes recursive function with no 'if' termination guard
Believes Python automatically stops recursion at 0
Fails to trace execution into negative numbers leading to RecursionError
taxonomies.common_reasoning: When n counts down, it reaches 0 and naturally stops recurring.
taxonomies.counterexample: Without 'if n <= 0: return', n becomes -1, -2, -3... until Python raises RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Trace recursive functions and identify termination conditions in unseen recursive patterns.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Correctly predicts call stack behavior and implements explicit base case checks.

taxonomies.name: Mutable Default Argument Aliasing
taxonomies.description: Learner assumes default parameter values (e.g. def add(x, lst=[])) are re-instantiated freshly upon every invocation.
observable_signals: Predicts list default is empty on second function call
Believes default argument expressions are evaluated at call-time rather than definition-time
Surprised when items appended in previous calls persist
taxonomies.common_reasoning: Each time we call add(1), lst defaults to a new empty list [], so the output is always [1].
taxonomies.counterexample: def add(x, lst=[]): the list [] is created ONCE when the function is defined. Successive calls mutate that exact same list object!
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Predict outputs of multiple sequential calls to functions with mutable default arguments.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Correctly anticipates default argument persistence and demonstrates idiomatic 'None' sentinel pattern.

taxonomies.name: While-Loop Mid-Body Termination
taxonomies.description: Learner believes a while loop terminates immediately mid-block the exact millisecond its conditional condition becomes false.
observable_signals: Predicts loop stops in the middle of executing body statements
Believes subsequent statements inside the current iteration are skipped as soon as condition variable flips
Fails to recognize that conditions are checked only at iteration boundary
taxonomies.common_reasoning: When x becomes 5 on line 3, the while condition x < 5 is false, so line 4 never executes.
taxonomies.counterexample: Python completes the entire body of the current iteration before re-evaluating the 'while' test at the top.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Trace while loops where the loop variable modifies before subsequent prints/actions in the same iteration.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Correctly executes full iteration bodies before checking loop exit conditions.

taxonomies.name: Integer Division Truncation
taxonomies.description: Learner confuses floor division (//) with float division (/) or expects // to round to the nearest integer rather than floor towards negative infinity.
observable_signals: Predicts 7 // 2 produces 3.5
Predicts -7 // 2 produces -3 instead of -4
Believes // rounds to nearest integer
taxonomies.counterexample: 7 // 2 is 3 (rounds DOWN to nearest integer). 7 / 2 is 3.5 (standard float division).
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Evaluate integer and float division expressions with positive and negative dividends.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Accurately predicts floor division vs float division across all numeric signs.

taxonomies.name: 1-Indexed Sequence Access
taxonomies.description: Learner assumes sequence indices start at 1 or treats negative indices as illegal syntax errors.
observable_signals: Predicts my_list[1] accesses the very first item
Predicts my_list[len(my_list)] returns the final item instead of IndexError
Believes my_list[-1] causes an out-of-bounds error
taxonomies.common_reasoning: The first element is at position 1, so items[1] returns the first element.
taxonomies.counterexample: Python uses 0-based indexing: items[0] is the 1st element, items[1] is the 2nd element, and items[-1] is the last element.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Query boundary elements, first element, and negative indices on sequences.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Consistently uses 0-based offsets and negative indexing correctly.

taxonomies.name: Boolean Operator Precedence
taxonomies.description: Learner evaluates boolean expressions strictly left-to-right, failing to respect that 'and' binds tighter than 'or'.
observable_signals: Groups 'A or B and C' as '(A or B) and C'
Ignores operator precedence hierarchy in boolean expressions
Predicts incorrect branch execution in compound conditionals
taxonomies.common_reasoning: Expressions are always read from left to right, so 'True or False and False' evaluates (True or False) which is True, and then True and False which is False.
taxonomies.counterexample: 'True or False and False' is evaluated as 'True or (False and False)' = 'True or False' = True, because 'and' has higher precedence than 'or'.
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Evaluate compound conditionals combining 'and', 'or', and 'not' without explicit parentheses.
taxonomies.resolution_criteria: Correctly applies operator precedence to compound logical expressions.

taxonomies.name: No Misconception / Correct Reasoning
taxonomies.description: Learner demonstrates sound mental models, accurate boundary understanding, and valid reasoning without detectable misconceptions.
observable_signals: Outputs match expected ground truth
Reasoning correctly states the underlying invariant or language rule
No evidence of faulty cognitive shortcuts or misinterpretations
taxonomies.assessment_strategy: Advance learner to higher difficulty challenges.
